staged_source_snapshot.description: This result directory retains the staged vulnerable OpenEXR checkout used by Stage 01 under `_work/src`. Its `src/lib/OpenEXRCore/validation.c` contains the crashing `internal_exr_validate_shared_attrs()` `memcmp` at line 740 and the matching `parse_header.c` call site at line 2675 cited by the saved AddressSanitizer trace; the staged patch hunk adds the missing attribute-type checks immediately before that sink in this same tree.

classification.classification_note: The reproduced failure is a crashing READ in `memcmp` during multipart shared-attribute validation. Source analysis shows a name-based type confusion: header parsing can accept an attribute whose name is `chromaticities` but whose declared on-disk type is `int`, and shared-attribute validation later dereferences the looked-up object through the `chromaticities` union arm without verifying `exr_attribute_t.type`.

bug_description.original: An invalid memory read (segmentation fault) occurs in internal_exr_validate_shared_attrs (src/lib/OpenEXRCore/validation.c). During header parsing (internal_exr_parse_header) the code invokes memcmp on attribute data that can reference out-of-bounds or uninitialized memory for crafted/malformed files, causing a crash. This can be triggered by attacker-supplied inputs and leads to denial-of-service during OpenEXR header validation.
bug_description.normalized: The staged PoC is an OpenEXR v2 multipart file. `internal_exr_parse_header()` consumes the file's version/flag word, enables multipart parsing, and later parses non-required attribute record(s) whose on-disk name is `chromaticities` but whose declared type string is `int`. Vulnerable `pull_attr()` therefore creates `exr_attribute_t` object(s) keyed by the name `chromaticities` while selecting the `EXR_ATTR_INT` layout and storing only a 4-byte integer payload. After multiple parts are parsed, `internal_exr_parse_header()` calls `internal_exr_validate_shared_attrs()` for part 1 against part 0. That routine looks up `chromaticities` in both compared parts by name only and falls through on lookup success without checking either returned object's `type` against `EXR_ATTR_CHROMATICITIES`. If either lookup result is one of the mis-typed `chromaticities`/`int` objects, the subsequent `memcmp(battr->chromaticities, cattr->chromaticities, sizeof(exr_attr_chromaticities_t))` dereferences the wrong union arm as a chromaticities pointer. The saved AddressSanitizer trace proves that this witness reaches that `memcmp` and crashes there, but the staged static evidence does not resolve whether `battr`, `cattr`, or both in the crashing `p = 1` comparison came from the witnessed malformed record(s).

source.description: First project-code consumption of attacker-controlled bytes on the crashing path. The parser reads the OpenEXR magic and version/flag word that later drives the multipart-only shared-attribute validation path.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` begins with bytes `76 2f 31 01 02 10 00 00`; `read_magic_and_flags()` consumes that header and materializes the version/flag word `0x00001002`, which contains the multipart bit used below.

sink.description: Crash sink. `memcmp` dereferences the looked-up attributes through the `chromaticities` union member even when one compared object is not actually `EXR_ATTR_CHROMATICITIES`, producing the saved invalid READ.

root_cause.description: Root cause fixed by the patch. This presence-only guard treats any two attributes found by the name `chromaticities` as layout-compatible and reaches `memcmp` without checking `battr->type` and `cattr->type` against `EXR_ATTR_CHROMATICITIES`.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific container gate. The saved PoC's version/flag word is `0x00001002`, so header parsing admits it as an OpenEXR v2 multipart file and enables the later cross-part shared-attribute validation path.

coarse_trace.summary: The parser reads the OpenEXR header flags, recognizes a multipart v2 file, and keeps the later shared-attribute comparison path reachable.

A non-required attribute named `chromaticities` is parsed with declared type string `int`, so OpenEXR allocates an `EXR_ATTR_INT` object that still carries the key `chromaticities` and stores only a 4-byte integer payload.
After multiple parts are parsed, the post-parse loop invokes `internal_exr_validate_shared_attrs()` to compare part 1 against part 0.

Shared-attribute validation looks up `chromaticities` by name only, misses the type check added by the patch, and crashes in `memcmp` while dereferencing the wrong union arm as `exr_attr_chromaticities_t`.

fine_trace.note: Source. The parser consumes the file header and materializes the version/flag word. On this witness the bytes encode `0x00001002`, which is the multipart v2 header state later required for the crashing path.

The parsed header flags set `ctxt->is_multipart = 1`, so the parser will continue into the multipart continuation and later run cross-part shared-attribute validation instead of terminating after a single header.
During header parsing, `pull_attr()` reads an attacker-controlled attribute name. The staged PoC contains a witnessed record whose parsed name is the exact string `chromaticities`.
The same record provides its declared on-disk type string. In the witnessed malformed record this string is `int`, not `chromaticities`.

fine_trace.code:
rv = exr_attr_list_add_by_type (
    ctxt, &(curpart->attributes), name, type, 0, NULL, &nattr);
fine_trace.note: Because `chromaticities` is not one of the required attributes handled by `check_req_attr()`, OpenEXR allocates a normal attribute by the attacker-supplied type string instead of by the semantic name.

The attribute factory matches the declared string `int` against the predefined type table and sets `nattr->type = EXR_ATTR_INT`. The object still retains the parsed name `chromaticities`, but its union layout is now the integer arm.

fine_trace.code:
rv = extract_attr_32bit (
    ctxt, scratch, &(nattr->i), name, type, attrsz, 1);
fine_trace.note: The parser follows the `EXR_ATTR_INT` switch arm and stores only a 4-byte integer payload into the attribute. After this step, one parsed part contains an attribute keyed by `chromaticities` whose concrete type is `EXR_ATTR_INT`.

fine_trace.code:
rv = internal_exr_validate_shared_attrs (ctxt,
                                         ctxt->parts[0],
                                         curp,
                                         p,
                                         mismatch,
                                         &mismatchcount);
fine_trace.note: After multiple part headers are parsed, the post-parse loop compares shared attributes for part `p = 1` against part 0. This call is only reached on the multipart path and is where the compared `chromaticities` attributes are fetched by name.

Root cause. `exr_get_attribute_by_name()` searches only by the string key `chromaticities`, and the guard accepts the path when both lookups succeed. No check verifies that either returned object actually has `type == EXR_ATTR_CHROMATICITIES`, so the later compare can receive a mis-typed `EXR_ATTR_INT` attribute from either compared part. The staged bytes prove such mis-typed `chromaticities` records exist in this witness, but do not statically identify which lookup result in the crashing `p = 1` call is malformed.

format.name: multipart OpenEXR v2 file
format.contract: An OpenEXR file with magic `20000630`, version/flag word `0x00001002` (v2 + multipart), and at least two parsed parts so `internal_exr_validate_shared_attrs()` compares part 1 against part 0. The witnessed trigger semantics are that the file contains parsed attribute record(s) keyed by `chromaticities` while declaring on-disk type `int`, and the multipart shared-attribute validator later performs name-only `chromaticities` lookups and reaches the unguarded `memcmp` for the part-1-versus-part-0 comparison. The staged evidence does not statically resolve whether the crashing `battr`, `cattr`, or both came from those malformed record(s).
